comparator.name: Biology
comparator.sourceNotes: The current official programme pages establish a coherent 180-EC Biology pathway. Year 1 contains 60 EC of broad compulsory biology, medical-biology, mathematics, statistics and research preparation. Year 2 contains 36 EC of compulsory study and 24 EC of domain-specialisation/elective space. Year 3 contains a 3-EC Biology Essay, 3 EC of Personal and Professional Development, 42 EC of domain-specialisation/elective space and a 12-EC research-department internship. The zero-credit introductory programme and Research Skills requirement remain compulsory but fall outside the 180-EC credit-bearing component list. The generic target offers seven named domain specialisations plus an eighth Free domain for students who do not want to select one domain; that least-specialised official option is selected independently of UCR fit, and its genuine profiling space is preserved rather than filled with invented courses.

comparatorRouteSelection.basis: The normalized target is the generic Biology bachelor. The official curriculum offers seven subject-specific domain specialisations and an eighth Free domain explicitly intended for students who cannot or do not want to select one domain. The Free domain is therefore the least specialised official continuation of the broad first-year foundation and is selected independently of UCR fit.

alternativeSelection.assessment: The closest programme preserves the broad span from organisms and ecosystems to molecules, human physiology, neuroscience and disease. The ecology/environment cluster and the human-biology/neurobiology cluster each support a coherent additional route. A separate microbiology, functional-genomics and physiological-adaptation candidate remains academically valid but cannot be added after the three-programme maximum is reached. notes.text: Both programmes cover substantial organismal, ecological, molecular, human and research biology. Radboud additionally requires dedicated work in plant evolution and physiology, microbiology and microbial metabolism, histology, two statistics courses, mathematics for biologists, scientific writing, extensive domain-specialisation space and a research-department internship. UCR can build broad, environmental and human-biological programmes, but it does not reproduce every specialist laboratory and organismal sequence.
